Name: reader_pays_writer_detours
Title: The Reader Pays the Writer's Detours: Consumer-Side Cost of Transferred Experience Tracks the Writer's Episode Length, Not Its Success
Short Hypothesis: The consumer-side cost of using a foreign experience pool (served tokens, generated and observation tokens and steps per episode) is inherited from the writer's trajectory length: a reader copies the step structure of the retrieved item, so on-policy self pools (long, with detours) cost more per successful episode than minimal expert walkthroughs at equal success. Pruning replay-verified detours from self items at fixed content removes the inherited cost without losing success, and padding expert walkthroughs with benign detours adds it; consequently the ranking of writers by gain per consumer token differs from their ranking by success, and cost-matched comparisons across writers must charge the reader's served tokens, not only the injected ones.
Related Work: Consumer-side inference tokens are not reported with transfer gains (digest gap G22): AMD (arxiv:2608.07169) omits student-side overhead, SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) compares raw trajectories and skills without matched per-reader token cost, memory-system profiling (arxiv:2606.24775) attributes cost to phases for a single writer, PAST-Bench (arxiv:2608.04003) and S3Gym (arxiv:2608.31100) report gains without the retention cost. AgentDiet (arxiv:2509.23586) reduces the agent's own context history to cut cost and inference-time distillation (arxiv:2512.02543) moves the ALFWorld cost-accuracy frontier with teacher demonstrations, but neither asks whether the reader's episode length depends on the retrieved item's length. MemoryCPT (arxiv:2608.04843) optimizes quality per inference cost within one writer-reader pair. In the home literature, Extraneousness-Aware Imitation Learning (arxiv:2210.01379) filters irrelevant segments from noisy demonstrations to recover performance, and 'What Demonstration Curation Metrics Do to Your Policy' (arxiv:2606.10229) shows defect detection and downstream policy quality decouple; both concern success, not inherited episode cost, and neither swaps the demonstrator. The archived idea abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) varied abstraction level within one writer on the success axis; here length is manipulated at fixed content with writer identity swapped and the outcome is the reader's cost.
Abstract: Transfer results report what the reader gains, not what the reader pays. We propose that the consumer-side cost of transferred experience is set by the writer's path length: LLM readers imitate the step structure of retrieved items, so a self pool of on-policy successes (which contain failed actions, 'Nothing happens' observations and revisits) makes the reader's own episodes longer than an expert walkthrough does, even when success is equal. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B as readers, the writer set is expert walkthroughs, Qwen3's own k=0 successes and EXAONE's own k=0 successes, all rendered in one action-observation format by environment replay and retrieved by one retriever whose ordering is fixed on the unmanipulated pools. Two content-preserving manipulations, applied to the retrieved items after retrieval and replay-verified, vary length at fixed content with a controlled dose: expert-padded inserts d benign detour steps (d drawn uniformly from 0 to 14 per game and seed, sampled from the self pool's detour distribution), and self-pruned removes every step whose replayed state diff is empty. A third arm, expert-corrupted, inserts detours that make the replayed walkthrough fail and is the positive control that the cells detect content damage. The manipulation cells run at 4 seeds (1,096 paired episodes per pair); we estimate the length-inheritance slope of the within-game, within-seed change in reader steps on the change in mean retrieved-item steps over all episodes with step-cap censoring modeled, and report success, steps, served tokens (all prompt and completion tokens the reader's replica processes per episode) and gain per 1k served tokens per writer x reader cell, net of k=0 and of the static3 prompt (Measurement C), together with the retained-gain ratio. Predictions: a slope of at least 0.3 in both manipulation pairs and for the foreign reader (expected SE 0.07 to 0.12, so a true slope near zero yields a CI upper bound below 0.3); pruning and padding within 6 net of their unmanipulated versions at a paired MDE of about 5.3 net; and a writer ranking by gain per served token that differs from the ranking by success, with the ratio's CI. The result gives transfer evaluation a cost axis on the reader's side and a cheap, replay-verified pruning step that any writer's pool can pass through before sharing.
Experiments: Preparation (CPU env replay, about half a day): render all pools into one action-observation item format by replaying the writer's actions; label every item step by its replayed state diff (empty diff, including 'Nothing happens' actions and revisits without change, = detour); build self-pruned (all empty-diff steps removed, replay-verified to still complete the task; items failing replay dropped and counted by writer); at read time build expert-padded (d detour steps, d uniform on 0..14 drawn per game and seed, sampled from the self pool's detour distribution and inserted at random positions between walkthrough actions, replay-verified) and expert-corrupted (every retrieved item receives d uniform on 1..14 state-changing detours, a take/put pair that relocates the task object, so the replayed walkthrough fails). Retrieval ordering is computed once on the unmanipulated pools and reused in every cell, so a manipulation changes only the injected items' content and length. Item lengths are logged (mean steps: expert, self-raw, self-pruned, expert-padded by dose, EXAONE-raw, EXAONE-pruned). Collection: EXAONE k=0 pool on the 3,553 train games (about 3 GPU-hours) on one A100 while the other serves the Qwen3 reader cells; each self pool is one k=0 pass per backbone over the same games, so foreign and self pools share the collection budget. Reader cells on the 274 eval games: 548 episodes per 2 seeds (about 30 min per replica), 1,096 per 4 seeds. Qwen3 reader at k=3, 4 seeds: expert (replayed), expert-padded, self-raw, self-pruned, expert-corrupted (5 x 1,096 = 5,480). Qwen3 reader at k=3, 2 seeds: EXAONE-raw, EXAONE-pruned, k=0 (2 seeds added to Measurement C's 2), static3 (2 seeds added), self-raw in the writer's native rendering (format control), expert-padded with observation text truncated to the unpadded item's token count and self-raw with observation text truncated to the pruned item's token count (token-matched length controls) (7 x 548 = 3,836). EXAONE reader at k=3, 4 seeds: Qwen3-raw, Qwen3-pruned, own-raw, own-pruned (4 x 1,096 = 4,384). EXAONE reader at k=3, 2 seeds: expert, k=0, static3 (3 x 548 = 1,644). Total 19 cells, 15,344 episodes, about 14 replica-hours plus the 3-hour collection, about 8.5 wall-hours on two A100s; the pre-registered contingency (2 more seeds on up to eight manipulation and neutrality cells, 4,384 episodes, about 4 replica-hours) keeps the study under 2 days. Per episode we log success, steps, generated tokens, observation tokens, injected tokens, prompt tokens per request (summed as served tokens), the retrieved items' ids, doses and step counts, and whether the step cap was hit. Analyses: (i) paired success differences per cell with bootstrap CIs over games, stratified by type; (ii) reader steps and served tokens per episode, all episodes with right-censoring at the step cap (Tobit) and successful-only; (iii) the length-inheritance slope per manipulation pair and reader: within-game, within-seed change in reader steps regressed on the change in mean retrieved-item steps, Tobit at the cap as primary and OLS on jointly successful episodes as secondary; (iv) gain per 1k served tokens with bootstrap CIs, and the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell (reader's gain from the writer's pool over the writer's own gain from the same pool, and over the reader's self-pool gain), in success and per served token; (v) the pruning rule scored by precision and recall of its step removals against the replayed state-diff labels.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 (4 seeds for the Qwen3 reader, 2 for EXAONE); static3, the best static-procedure prompt of Measurement C (3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, about 430 tokens), at 4 seeds for Qwen3 and 2 for EXAONE, every gain reported net of it; the wrong-type placebo blind1 reused from Measurement C (paired on the same games and seeds, no rerun); self-pool control at matched collection cost (each reader's own k=0 pass over the same 3,553 train games as the foreign pool); retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell with CIs; expert-corrupted as the manufactured, positively controlled contamination arm (Gate 0: its harm must be at least 6 net for the neutrality cells to count as sensitive); token-matched length controls (padded items with observation text truncated to the unpadded token count; raw self items truncated to the pruned token count) to separate item steps from item tokens, which also compares the adaptation step (pruning) with direct injection of the unmodified item at matched tokens; native-rendering control for the self pool (writer's own reasoning text kept, item steps unchanged) to show format does not carry the length effect; the k=3 vs k=7 injected-token difference of Measurement C (430 vs 1,010 tokens) as the accounting positive control. Cut from the previous version because they carried no prediction: the k=1 cells, random-deletion pruning (replaced by the state-diff labels and by the padding pair, which varies length in the opposite direction with content held fixed) and the own-vs-other detour-source padding.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline, length inheritance): for the Qwen3 reader at k=3, in each manipulation pair (expert vs expert-padded, dose 0..14; self-raw vs self-pruned), the within-game, within-seed change in reader steps regressed on the change in mean retrieved-item steps over all 1,096 paired episodes (Tobit at the step cap) has a slope of at least 0.3 with a 95% CI lower bound above 0.1. Falsifier: the slope's 95% CI upper bound is below 0.3 in either pair (the reader plans from the item rather than copying its path). Reachable: with 1,096 pairs, a residual SD of about 10 steps and an item-step-change SD of 4.3 (padding) or about 2.5 (pruning, pilot-estimated), the SE is about 0.07 and 0.12, so a true slope of 0 gives an upper bound of about 0.14 and 0.24, and a true slope of 0.1 is rejected in the padding pair with power about 0.8; the achieved SE is reported and the contingency seeds are pre-registered. Arm: the four manipulation cells at 4 seeds; injected tokens rise with padding by construction and are excluded from this estimand. P2 (pruning is success-neutral): in both readers at 4 seeds, self-pruned minus self-raw lies within 6 net with the 90% CI inside [-6, +6] (paired MDE about 5.3 net). Falsifier: pruned at least 6 net below raw with the 95% CI excluding 0, the outcome the cue-discarding account of arxiv:2605.24117 predicts; arm: the pruned vs raw cells (Qwen3 own pair, EXAONE own pair). P3 (padding is success-neutral, gated): expert-padded minus expert lies within 6 net (90% CI inside [-6, +6]) while expert-corrupted is at least 6 net below expert (the positive control). Falsifier: padded at least 6 net below expert with CI excluding 0 (detours contaminate content, not only cost); if the corrupted arm fails to reach 6 net harm the cell is declared insensitive and P3 is reported as untested, not confirmed; arm: expert-padded, expert-corrupted and expert cells. P4 (cost reranks writers): for the Qwen3 reader, gain per 1k served tokens (net success over k=0 divided by mean served tokens per episode, bootstrap CI over games) of the expert pool exceeds that of self-raw by at least 25% with the ratio's 95% CI lower bound above 1.0, while the paired success gains of the two pools are within 8 net. Falsifier: the ratio's CI upper bound is at most 1.0 (self-raw's gain per served token is at least the expert's), or the success gap is at least 8 net with CI excluding 0 so that the cost ranking merely follows success; arm: expert vs self-raw cells at 4 seeds with token accounting. P5 (foreign reader inherits, no self-recognition): EXAONE reading Qwen3-raw vs Qwen3-pruned at 4 seeds (same estimand and count as P1) shows a slope of at least 0.3, and within the EXAONE reader the slope on its own pair (own-raw vs own-pruned, 4 seeds) minus the slope on the Qwen3 pair has a 95% CI that includes 0 (SE of the difference about 0.17). Falsifiers, each with its own CI and neither conditional on P1's outcome: (a) the Qwen3-pair slope's CI upper bound is below 0.3; (b) the own-minus-foreign slope difference is at least 0.2 with its CI excluding 0 (inheritance is partly self-recognition); arm: the four EXAONE 4-seed cells; the Qwen3 reader's EXAONE-raw vs EXAONE-pruned pair at 2 seeds is reported as a wider-CI replication. None is entailed: the reader may ignore item structure (P1, P5), detours may carry object-location cues (P2), inserted detours may mislead (P3), and cost may simply track success (P4); P4's token gap is partly produced by P1's slope, but P4 fails independently whenever self-raw's success gain exceeds the expert's by 8 net or its per-token ratio is not above 1.
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells are paired on the same 274 games with the same retrieval ordering; bootstrap over games, stratified by type. Success: Measurement C's paired CI half-width at 274 x 2 seeds is about 5.25 net (SE 2.7), the 8-net floor of the brief; the neutrality cells run at 4 seeds, where episode-level noise halves in variance (SE about 1.9, half-width 3.7, MDE about 5.3 net at 80% power), so the 6-net margin is above the resolvable MDE; the achieved SE is computed from the data and, if the achieved MDE exceeds 6 net, the neutrality cells get 2 more seeds from the contingency rather than the margin being reported as met. Cross-writer success differences keep the 8-net margin. Slope: the estimand is the within-game, within-seed paired difference, so eval-game difficulty cancels; the dose design (d uniform on 0..14, drawn per game and seed) makes the item-step change vary within game across seeds; expected SE 0.07 (padding) and 0.12 (pruning) at 1,096 pairs, from residual SD about 10 steps (all episodes) and item-step-change SD 4.3 and 2.5; after the first 2 seeds the achieved SDs are used to project the 4-seed SE and, if it exceeds 0.08 (padding) or 0.14 (pruning), the manipulation cells extend to 6 seeds within the contingency budget. Censoring: reader steps are right-censored at the run's step cap; the slope is estimated by Tobit on all episodes (primary) and by OLS on jointly successful episodes (secondary), and the censoring fraction per cell is reported. Cost: served tokens are the sum of prompt and completion tokens over all requests in an episode from the vLLM usage fields; generated, observation and injected tokens are also summed per episode, and injected tokens are reported separately so the by-construction part of any cost change is visible. Order: k=0, static3 and the unmanipulated writers first; manipulation cells only after the replayed expert cell reproduces Measurement C's k3 within 8 net (k3 minus static3 = +17.2, CI about +/-5). Throughput and queue occupancy per replica are logged; the EXAONE collection overlaps the Qwen3 reader cells so both A100s stay busy.

Q6 (closest named method, channel: s2cli S2+HF, hits from hf): 'raw trajectory reuse versus distilled skills inference token cost per-episode compute agent memory' -> SkillEvolBench 2605.24117 (raw beats skills, no per-reader token matching), MemoryCPT 2608.04843 (cost-aware memory construction, single writer), Evidence Over Plans 2605.09192 (efficient skills, low inference cost), 2605.12978 (consolidated memories become faulty), Activity Frames 2608.05784, AgentDiet. No preprint found that reports a length-inheritance effect from retrieved experience or a writer ranking by gain per consumer token.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Replay verification requires deterministic ALFWorld replays; items that fail replay are dropped and the drop rate by writer and manipulation is reported (a high rate would bias the pruned pool toward simpler items, checked by comparing type and length distributions). The pruning rule uses replayed state diffs, but a detour with an empty state diff can still carry an object-location cue; P2 tests that directly and the padding pair varies length in the other direction. The step cap censors long episodes; the Tobit estimate assumes a latent normal step count and is reported alongside the successful-only estimate. Item tokens and item steps co-vary; the token-matched controls truncate observation text, which is itself a manipulation, and are reported as controls, not as primary cells. The pruning-pair lever (item-step-change SD about 2.5) is weaker than the padding lever, so its slope has a wider CI; the contingency seeds are budgeted for it. The retained-gain ratio has a wide CI when the writer's own gain is small. EXAONE serving is unverified (fallback gpt-oss-120b, which changes the foreign-reader cells' cost but not the design). No proximity claim is made: P5 predicts the absence of a self-recognition effect on the slope, so the capability-versus-proximity separation of the brief is not invoked. Only ALFWorld is used; in environments with cheap steps the cost consequence is small even if inheritance holds, and the reranking in P4 depends on the success gaps measured here.
Addresses gap: G22 (consumer-side inference-token and per-episode cost reported with the gain, cost-matched across writers and manipulated at fixed content).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: 'Injected tokens ~140/430/1,010 at k=1/3/7' reports only injected tokens for one writer; this idea claims the dominant consumer-side cost is generated steps inherited from the writer's path and manipulates that path at fixed content across writers. Digest card arxiv:2605.24117 finds raw trajectories beat distilled skills on success in a single-writer setting without per-reader token cost; this idea claims the raw trajectory's success advantage comes with an inherited cost that pruning removes without losing success, with writer identity swapped. Archived abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs varied abstraction level within one writer on the success axis; pruning and padding are not abstraction (content is held fixed and replay-verified), the outcome is the reader's cost, and the writer is manipulated.
Changes made: P1: manipulation-pair cells raised from 2 to 4 seeds (1,096 paired episodes per pair); padding given a per-game, per-seed dose (0..14 detour steps) so the item-step change varies within game and the lever SD is 4.3; primary slope estimated on all episodes with step-cap censoring modeled (Tobit), successful-only as secondary, so cap-hitting detour-copying episodes are kept; falsifier restated as the CI upper bound below the claimed 0.3 (a true zero slope reaches it at SE 0.07 to 0.12), with the SE arithmetic stated and a pre-registered contingency to 6 seeds. P2 and P3: neutrality cells at 4 seeds so the paired MDE (about 5.3 net) is below the 6-net margin; equivalence stated as a 90% CI inside [-6, +6]; rule added that the margin is met by evidence, not insensitivity (seeds added if the achieved MDE exceeds 6). P3: expert-corrupted arm added (replay-failing detours at the same dose) as the positive control that the cell detects content damage at the Gate-0 level; P3 gated on it. P4: cost measure changed to served tokens (all prompt and completion tokens the reader processes), bootstrap CI added to the gain-per-token ratio, confirm requires the ratio's CI lower bound above 1. P5: EXAONE manipulation pair at 4 seeds (same count as the self reader); falsifier restated as two outcomes with their own CIs (foreign-pair slope upper bound below 0.3; within-reader own-minus-foreign slope difference at least 0.2 with CI excluding 0), no longer conditional on P1. Binding rules: retained-gain ratio per writer x reader cell added; self-pool control at matched collection cost stated; pruning rule scored by precision and recall against replayed state-diff labels; retrieval ordering fixed on the unmanipulated pools. Cut to fit the envelope: k=1 cells, random-deletion pruning, own-vs-other detour-source padding. Claim kept as sharp: the slope threshold (0.3), the neutrality margin (6 net, now resolvable), the 25% reranking and the foreign-reader inheritance are unchanged; the one softening refused was lowering the slope threshold to what 2 seeds could detect, answered instead with seeds and a dose design.
